open_questions: Only sector 51 used for centroid (seasons predicts others); single-sector off-target 3.6" at 3.4 sigma needs multi-sector centroid to rule out blend.

Phase curve amplitude 11480 ppm (~30% of dip) and transit_depths p_consistent 1.71e-05 (chi2 49.06/15 dof) plus secondary snr 7.833 at phase 0.4016 need RV to confirm M dwarf planetary mass and spot-check; stellar RUWE 1.333 and excess_noise_sig 5.393 also warrant binarity test
dossier.public_summary: A 0.49-hour deep (about 3%) dip repeats every 0.636 days 16 times with a flat bottom on a small M dwarf, implying a ~7 Earth-radius short-period planet if on target. Odd/even and secondary checks show no sign of an eclipsing binary and no nearby star can plausibly mimic the dip. A bright out-of-eclipse swing likely reflects the star's own variability but also leaves an unresolved phase-curve and a mild single-sector centroid offset (~3.6 arcsec) that need further photometry and radial velocities.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed (negative v_sigma) favors a transiting planet over a V-shaped grazing binary on 1 sector.
Radius is planet-sized on the M dwarf (rp/r* 0.1967) with no positive evidence for a stellar companion, despite phase-curve and secondary excess.
Odd/even depths identical (0.5938 sigma) and secondary at phase 0.4016 is far from half-orbit (snr_at_half 0.384), no alias at 2x; hot binary signature absent.

Difference imaging puts dip 3.6" off but no catalogued neighbour within 1px can plausibly cause it (neighbours plausible_within_1px 0, closest 31.9" needs 0.4667 eclipse) and only one sector available, so I cannot verify on-target; off-target is 3.4 sigma, not strong, and both stars and known planets appear off-target by about this amount.
reasons.value: off_target 3.576" (3.4 sigma) with suspects 78.5 sigma away

reasons.why: No star inside a TESS pixel that could produce the 38500 ppm dip with ≤25% eclipse; closest plausible 31.9" away needs 46% eclipse inconsistent with broadband colour offset.
Depth does not change between sectors (only sector 51) and transit_depths shows consistent individual depths (share_of_top_3 0.307, 16 transits), so not a few bad events.

Large out-of-transit swing favors spotted/variable star or very close binary, but on a Teff 3374 K active M dwarf a ~0.6d ultra-short-period planet can also show strong phase modulation; with flat shape and no secondary/half-period signal the planet explanation remains the best, though remaining double-dip is an open question.
